text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for people who did not write it. One key part of clean code is following naming conventions. When you choose clear and meaningful names for variables and functions, other developers can quickly see what your code does. Functions should also be small and do only one job, which makes them simpler to test and reuse. Finally, clean code is easier to maintain. When you need to fix a bug or add a new feature, well-organized code saves you time and reduces mistakes.
